title: Alcohol and Your Health
hook: There's no amount of alcohol proven to be good for you — but there's a meaningful difference between a glass with dinner and patterns that quietly raise your risk of cancer, liver disease, and more.
key_points: Less is better: when it comes to health risk, no drinking is the safest choice.
A U.S. standard drink is roughly 12 oz beer, 5 oz wine, or 1.5 oz spirits.
Moderate use is defined as up to 1 drink a day for women, 2 for men.
Heavy and binge drinking raise risk of liver disease, several cancers, and high blood pressure.
If cutting back is hard, that itself is worth talking to a clinician about.
content_html: It's tempting to look for a "safe" or even healthy level of drinking, but the honest answer from public-health agencies is that less is better, and not drinking at all is the lowest-risk option. The size of the risk depends heavily on how much and how often you drink.
extra_html: The CDC describes moderate drinking as up to one drink a day for women and up to two for men, where a standard drink is roughly 12 ounces of beer, 5 ounces of wine, or 1.5 ounces of distilled spirits — amounts that all carry a comparable dose of pure alcohol. Heavy drinking and binge drinking are a different story: over time they raise the risk of liver disease, high blood pressure, and several cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, along with injuries and dependence. People who don't drink shouldn't start for supposed health benefits. And if cutting back feels harder than it should, that's a meaningful signal worth raising with a clinician rather than a personal failing.

source.name: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

related.title: Understanding Addiction
related.hook: Addiction isn't a lack of willpower or a moral failing — it's a treatable medical condition that changes how the brain works. And like other chronic illnesses, it responds to treatment.

related.title: Understanding Blood Pressure
related.hook: High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' for a reason — it usually has no symptoms, yet it quietly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke.

related.title: Cancer Screenings Worth Knowing
related.hook: Screening looks for cancer before symptoms start — and for a few common cancers, that early catch dramatically improves the odds.

flashcards.prompt: How does the CDC define moderate drinking?

choices.text: Up to 1 drink a day for women and 2 for men
Up to 3 drinks a day for anyone

flashcards.explanation_html: Moderate drinking is defined as up to 1 drink per day for women and up to 2 drinks per day for men, on days when alcohol is consumed.

flashcards.prompt: Roughly how much alcohol counts as one U.S. standard drink?
flashcards.back_html: About 12 oz of regular beer, 5 oz of wine, or 1.5 oz of distilled spirits — each contains a similar amount of pure alcohol.
